verses.text: Joseph couldn’t hold it in anymore with everyone standing there. He called out, “Everybody, step outside!” Once they were alone, he revealed himself to his brothers. The moment had arrived. 😭
Joseph cried so loudly the Egyptians heard him, and word reached Pharaoh’s house too. The whole palace knew something major was happening. 😢
Joseph said, “I’m Joseph! Is my father still alive?” His brothers couldn’t answer. They were shook, standing right in front of him. 😳
He said, “Please, come closer.” They moved in, and he told them, “I’m Joseph, your brother—the one you sold into Egypt.” No hiding from the truth now. 🫂
“Don’t be crushed or mad at yourselves for selling me here. God sent me ahead of you to keep people alive.” Joseph gave them the bigger picture. 🙏
“The famine has already lasted two years, and there are still five more years with no plowing and no harvest.” The hard season wasn’t over yet. 🌾
“God sent me ahead of you to keep a remnant alive on earth and rescue your family through a great deliverance.” Their survival had a purpose. 🕊️
“So it wasn’t ultimately you who sent me here—God did. He made me like a father to Pharaoh, lord over his whole household, and ruler across Egypt.” Joseph’s position had changed completely. 👑
“Hurry back to my father and tell him, ‘Your son Joseph says: God has made me lord over all Egypt. Come down to me—don’t delay.’” The reunion couldn’t wait. 🏃
“You’ll settle in Goshen, close to me—you, your children, grandchildren, flocks, herds, and everything you own.” Joseph was making room for the whole family. 🏠
“I’ll provide for you there, because five famine years are still coming. Otherwise you, your household, and all you have could end up in poverty.” He had a real plan to care for them. 🧺
“You can see with your own eyes—and Benjamin can too—that it’s really me speaking to you.” No messenger, no rumor: Joseph himself. 👀
“Tell my father about all my honor in Egypt and everything you’ve seen. Then hurry and bring him down here.” Joseph wanted his father with him. 💌
Joseph threw his arms around Benjamin and wept; Benjamin wept against him too. They held on and let it all out. 😭
Then Joseph kissed every one of his brothers and cried with them. After that, they finally started talking together. The wall came down. 🫂
News reached Pharaoh’s house: “Joseph’s brothers have arrived.” Pharaoh and his officials were pleased to hear it. Good news was spreading fast. 🏛️
Pharaoh told Joseph, “Tell your brothers: load up your animals and travel back to Canaan.” The king was sending them home with a mission. 🐪
“Bring your father and your households back to me. I’ll give you the best of Egypt, and you’ll eat from the richest part of the land.” Pharaoh opened the door wide. 🌾
“Here’s what you must do: take wagons from Egypt for your children and wives, bring your father, and come back.” They’d have a way to move everyone. 🛞
“Don’t stress about your belongings. The best of all Egypt is yours.” Pharaoh made sure they knew they’d be provided for. 🎁
Israel’s sons did as told. Joseph supplied wagons by Pharaoh’s command and gave them provisions for the journey. They wouldn’t travel empty-handed. 🧳
Joseph gave each brother a change of clothes. Benjamin got five changes and three hundred pieces of silver—extra honor for his younger brother. 👕
He sent his father ten donkeys loaded with Egypt’s finest goods, plus ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread, and supplies for the road. Jacob would have what he needed. 🫏
Joseph sent his brothers off and said, “Don’t start quarrelling on the way.” He knew the trip home could bring old arguments back up. 🛣️
They left Egypt and arrived in Canaan, back with their father Jacob. The news was about to change his whole world. 🏠
They told him, “Joseph is alive! He rules all Egypt!” Jacob’s heart nearly stopped; he couldn’t believe them at first. 😲
They repeated everything Joseph had said, and when Jacob saw the wagons Joseph had sent to bring him, his spirit came alive again. Hope returned. ✨
Israel said, “That’s enough—I know Joseph my son is alive. I’m going to see him before I die.” At last, the family was coming back together. 🥹
